newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish debt/GDP ratio 73.3 pct at end-1996 -NTMA.
newsitem.headline: Irish debt/GDP ratio 73.3 pct at end-1996 -NTMA.

text.p: The ratio of Ireland's general government debt to GDP fell 8.3 percentage points in 1996 to an estimated 73.3 percent at the end of the year, the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said on Tuesday.
The NTMA, a state agency which manages Ireland's national debt, said the general government debt was estimated at 32.3 billion Irish pounds at end-1996, compared with 32.7 billion at the end of 1995.

The reduction was due principally to substantial positive foreign exchange movements, which cut the debt by 859 million Irish pounds and more than offset a "relatively low" government borrowing requirement, the NTMA said.
The reduction in debt, coupled with strong economic growth, led to the large reduction in the debt/GDP ratio, it said.
The general government debt/GDP ratio is a key element of the European Union's Maastricht criteria for qualification for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

According to the Maastricht rules, the ratio should not exceed 60 percent, but a country can still qualify for EMU if its ratio exceeds this but is deemed to be declining substantially and continuously.
The NTMA said its gross repayments of foreign debt came to 1.349 billion Irish pounds in 1996 compared with 672 million in 1995.
